description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/sselect.t's rows `select "a" $blank $blank 0` (and the two positions
after it) hand 4-argument `select` an ordinary string as the read / write /
exception bit vector.  perl accepts it -- a bit vector IS a string -- and
returns 0 ready descriptors; PCL fails the row.

The three wide-character rows of the same file are separate and already
NS:Unicode semantics differences (perl croaks on a bit vector holding a
character above 0xFF).

`perl-tests`' op/lex_assign.t row 106 ("sselect") is the same call and moves
with it.

Read `%p-select-4arg` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): the fdmask read/writeback pair is
already there, so this is about what it ACCEPTS, not about the select itself.
subject: 4-argument `select` rejects a plain string where perl accepts it as a bit vector (op/sselect.t, 3 rows; op/lex_assign.t 1)
